newsitem.title: INDIA: Schlumberger sets up Indian subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Schlumberger sets up Indian subsidiary.

text.p: Global engineering services company Schlumberger Ltd said on Wednesday it had set up a 100 percent-owned Indian subsidiary with an eye on the domestic banking and telecommunication industries.
Schlumberger Measurement and Systems India Ltd, with an initial investment of $10 million, will be headquartered in New Delhi, officials said.

"The India unit will focus on electronic transactions products for the banking and telecommunication industry," Sanjaya Sood, managing director of Schlumberger Measurement and Systems India Ltd, told Reuters.
Chief executive officer, Dugald Euan Baird told a news conference that the Indian market offered tremendous growth potential for Schlumberger's products.

"We believe that electronic transaction products have a tremendous market potential in India," Baird said. "There will be over two billion smart cards in circulation by the year 2000. A sizeable portion of that will be in India."
Liberalisation of the Indian economy offered more business opportunities for the company, he said.
India liberalised its economy in 1991, as part of an economic reforms programme launched by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, by dismantling decades old socialist controls.
"The strength of India is that it has a proper consultative democratic process which means changes take place rather slowly but they take place surely," Baird told Reuters.
He hoped India would catch up in 10 years with rapidly growing East Asian economies.
The group was also in the process of setting up a research and development centre and a computer software facility at Gurgaon near the Indian capital of Delhi, he added.
Schlumberger, a worldwide group with a big presence in Europe, has interests in engineering and services linked to electronic instruments, oil exploration and telecommunications.
